title: Version-correlated regression after a rollout
tell: Onset is a step, not a ramp: a build either has the defect or it does not, so the transition is as fast as the rollout reaches each task.
The change concentrates on a version label rather than on a region or cell, and the affected cells are exactly those the rollout has reached.
Traffic is flat across the onset. A rollout changes how requests are served, not how many arrive.
Jobs sharing the rolled binary degrade together while co-located jobs on the old build stay healthy, which is what distinguishes this from a cell-wide fault.

confusable_with.discriminator: A cell fault hits every job in the cell including ones the rollout never touched. Check whether an un-rolled job in the same cell is also degraded.
A rollout landing near onset is not proof. The claim only holds if un-rolled cells show no onset; if they do, the rollout is a bystander.
